title: Command Injection via Windows Shell Metacharacters in desktop_open_url
description: The desktop_open_url Tauri command on Windows invokes cmd.exe /c start with unquoted user-controlled URL arguments, allowing shell metacharacters such as & and | to escape argument boundaries and execute arbitrary host commands.
root_cause: frontend/src-tauri/src/lib.rs invokes std::process::Command::new("cmd").args(["/c", "start", "", &url]). Because Rust standard library only automatically quotes arguments on Windows when whitespace is present, URLs containing & are parsed by cmd.exe as command separators.
intended_behavior: The application should open external HTTP/HTTPS URLs directly via the operating system shell handler (rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler) and strictly reject URLs containing control characters or shell quotes.

trace.description: URL received from renderer via Tauri IPC invocation
URL parsed and verified for http/https scheme without validating shell metacharacters
Unquoted URL passed as argument to cmd.exe /c start

conditions.description: Running on Microsoft Windows host where cmd.exe parses & as command separator
User or renderer triggers external URL navigation containing shell metacharacters

execution.attacker_perspective: Compromised webview or malicious external link passed to desktop_open_url IPC
instructions: Invoke desktop_open_url with payload https://example.com/?q=1&calc.exe on Windows
execution.observed_result: cmd.exe splits on & and executes calc.exe in the user context

remediation.strategy: Replace cmd.exe invocation with rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler and validate that URLs contain no control or quote characters.

likelihood.reason: Requires either webview XSS or malicious URL passed through update / external link triggers

impact.reason: Arbitrary command execution on host Windows system in user context

confidence.reason: Demonstrated through Rust standard library Windows argument quoting mechanics and cmd.exe behavior
